title: Cambridge 14 · Test 2

sents: Alexander Henderson was born in Scotland in 1831 and was the son of a successful merchant.
His grandfather, also called Alexander, had founded the family business, and later became the first chairman of the National Bank of Scotland.
The family had extensive landholding in Scotland.
Besides its residence in Edinburgh, it owned Press Estate, 650 acres of farmland about 35 miles southeast of the city.

The family often stayed at Press Castle, the large mansion on the northern edge of the property, and Alexander spent much of his childhood in the area, playing on the beach near Eyemouth or fishing in the streams nearby.

simp.text: Henderson was born / was the son of a merchant
grandfather founded the business, became chairman
family had landholding
it owned Press Estate
Alexander spent much of his childhood in the area
simp.note: Bỏ playing…, fishing…, đồng vị the large mansion…

paras.conn: ① cha là thương nhân → ② ông nội lập doanh nghiệp (cùng nhà) → ③④ gia đình có nhiều đất → ⑤ Alexander lớn lên ở đó. Mạch: **gia đình giàu → có đất → cậu bé gắn bó với nơi này**.
paras.main: Henderson xuất thân từ gia đình thương nhân giàu có và **sống nhiều ở Press Estate thuở nhỏ**.
warn: ⚠️ Q1 nói `rarely visited`, trái với ⑤ `spent much of his childhood in the area`.

sents: Even after he went to school at Murcheston Academy on the outskirts of Edinburgh, Henderson returned to Press at weekends.
In 1849 he began a three-year apprenticeship to become an accountant.
Although he never liked the prospect of a business career, he stayed with it to please his family.
In October 1855, however, he emigrated to Canada with his wife Agnes Elder Robertson and they settled in Montreal.

simp.text: Henderson returned to Press at weekends
simp.note: Bỏ Even after he went to school…

simp.text: he began an apprenticeship
he stayed with it to please his family
simp.note: Although… = điều không thích, không phải ý chính

simp.text: he emigrated to Canada
simp.note: Bỏ with his wife…; however báo hướng mới

paras.conn: ① vẫn về Press cuối tuần (xác nhận Q1) → ②③ học kế toán dù không thích, vì gia đình → ④ **however** sang Canada. Mạch: **học theo ý gia đình → rồi rời Scotland**.
paras.main: Henderson theo nghề kế toán **để làm hài lòng gia đình** rồi di cư sang Canada năm 1855.
warn: ⚠️ `Although he never liked` dễ khiến chọn FALSE ở Q2; ý chính nằm sau dấu phẩy.

sents: Henderson learned photography in Montreal around the year 1857 and quickly took it up as a serious amateur.
He became a personal friend and colleague of the Scottish-Canadian photographer William Notman.
The two men made a photographic excursion to Niagara Falls in 1860 and they cooperated on experiments with magnesium flares as a source of artificial light in 1865.
They belonged to the same societies and were among the founding members of the Art Association of Montreal.
Henderson acted as chairman of the association's first meeting, which was held in Notman's studio on 11 January 1860.

simp.text: Henderson learned photography, took it up
He became friend of Notman
men made an excursion, cooperated on experiments
simp.note: Bỏ to Niagara Falls, as a source of…

simp.text: They belonged to societies, were founding members
Henderson acted as chairman

paras.conn: ①② học nghề rồi kết bạn với Notman → ③ cùng đi chụp, cùng thí nghiệm → ④⑤ cùng lập hội. Mạch: **hợp tác nhiều mặt**.
paras.main: Henderson và Notman là **bạn và đồng nghiệp thân thiết**.
warn: ⚠️ Q3 hỏi họ `surprised by the results`. ③ chỉ nói họ **cooperated on experiments**; thiếu kết quả và cảm xúc → NG.

sents: In spite of their friendship, their styles of photography were quite different.
While Notman's landscapes were noted for their bold realism, Henderson for the first 20 years of his career produced romantic images, showing the strong influence of the British landscape tradition.
His artistic and technical progress was rapid and in 1865 he published his first major collection of landscape photographs.
The publication had limited circulation (only seven copies have ever been found), and was called Canadian Views and Studies.
The contents of each copy vary significantly and have proved a useful source for evaluating Henderson's early work.

simp.text: styles were quite different
simp.note: In spite of X, Y: Y chính

simp.text: Henderson produced romantic images
simp.note: While A, B: B chính; bỏ showing…

simp.text: progress was rapid; he published collection
publication had limited circulation
contents vary, have proved useful

paras.conn: ① khác phong cách → ② đối chiếu: Notman thực tế, Henderson lãng mạn → ③④⑤ bộ ảnh đầu tiên 1865. Mạch: **bạn thân nhưng khác nghề → sản phẩm riêng**.
paras.main: Dù là bạn, **hai người có phong cách chụp khác nhau**.

sents: In 1866, he gave up his business to open a photographic studio, advertising himself as a portrait and landscape photographer.
From about 1870 he dropped portraiture to specialize in landscape photography and other views.

His numerous photographs of city life revealed in street scenes, houses, and markets are alive with human activity, and although his favourite subject was landscape he usually composed his scenes around such human pursuits as farming the land, cutting ice on a river, or sailing down a woodland stream.
There was sufficient demand for these types of scenes and others he took depicting the lumber trade, steamboats and waterfalls to enable him to make a living.
There was little competing hobby or amateur photography before the late 1880s because of the time-consuming techniques involved and the weight of equipment.

People wanted to buy photographs as souvenirs of a trip or as gifts, and catering to this market, Henderson had stock photographs on display at his studio for mounting, framing, or inclusion in albums.

simp.text: he gave up business to open a studio
he dropped portraiture to specialize in landscape
simp.note: Giữ mục đích to specialize… vì Q6

simp.text: photographs are alive with human activity; he composed scenes around human pursuits
demand was sufficient to enable him to make a living
amateur photography was little because of time-consuming techniques and the weight of equipment
simp.note: Bỏ before the late 1880s; giữ lý do

simp.text: People wanted to buy photographs as souvenirs or gifts; Henderson had stock photographs

paras.conn: ① mở studio → ② bỏ chân dung, chuyên phong cảnh → ③ ảnh có cảnh sinh hoạt → ④ đủ khách để sống → ⑤ ít đối thủ nghiệp dư vì kỹ thuật tốn thời gian và thiết bị nặng → ⑥ khách mua làm quà → ông bán ảnh có sẵn. Mạch: **chuyên môn hóa → có thị trường → ít cạnh tranh**.
paras.main: Henderson **chuyển sang phong cảnh** và kiếm sống nhờ nhu cầu ảnh làm quà, ít đối thủ nghiệp dư.
warn: ⚠️ Q5: ① chỉ nói `open a photographic studio`, không nói vị trí → NG.

sents: Henderson frequently exhibited his photographs in Montreal and abroad, in London, Edinburgh, Dublin, Paris, New York, and Philadelphia.
He met with greater success in 1877 and 1878 in New York when he won first prizes in the exhibition held by E and H T Anthony and Company for landscapes using the Lambertype process.
In 1878 his work won second prize at the world exhibition in Paris.

simp.text: Henderson frequently exhibited photographs
He met with greater success; won first prizes
work won second prize

paras.conn: ① triển lãm thường xuyên → ② thành công lớn ở New York → ③ giải nhì ở Paris. Mạch: **hoạt động → thành tựu**.
paras.main: Henderson **triển lãm nhiều nơi và giành giải**. (Đoạn này không có câu hỏi.)

sents: In the 1890s [1870s] and 1880s Henderson travelled widely throughout Quebec and Ontario, in Canada, documenting the major cities of the two provinces and many of the villages in Quebec.
He was especially fond of the wilderness and often travelled by canoe on the Blanche, du Lièvre, and other noted eastern rivers.
He went on several occasions to the Maritimes and in 1872 he sailed by yacht along the lower north shore of the St Lawrence River.
That same year, while in the lower St Lawrence River region, he took some photographs of the construction of the Intercolonial Railway.
This undertaking led in 1875 to a commission from the railway to record the principal structures along the almost-completed line connecting Montreal to Halifax.
Commissions from other railways followed.
In 1876 he photographed bridges on the Quebec, Montreal, Ottawa and Occidental Railway between Montreal and Ottawa.
In 1885 he went west along the Canadian Pacific Railway (CPR) as far as Rogers Pass in British Columbia, where he took photographs of the mountains and the progress of construction.

simp.text: Henderson travelled widely throughout Quebec and Ontario
He often travelled by canoe on eastern rivers
simp.note: Bỏ was fond of…, tên sông

simp.text: He went to the Maritimes; sailed by yacht
simp.note: Giữ yacht để thấy là bẫy

simp.text: he took photographs of the construction
undertaking led to a commission to record structures along the almost-completed line
Commissions followed
he photographed bridges
he went west; took photographs of the mountains and progress of construction
simp.note: Giữ of the mountains vì Q13

paras.conn: ① đi khắp miền đông → ②③ đi bằng canoe (sông) và yacht (biển) → ④ chụp công trình đường sắt → ⑤ nhận ủy thác → ⑥⑦ thêm các tuyến khác → ⑧ đi phía tây. Mạch: **du hành → đường sắt**.
paras.main: Henderson **đi khắp nơi và nhận nhiều ủy thác chụp đường sắt**.
warn: ⚠️ Q12: `canoe` (②, sông miền đông) ≠ `yacht` (③, bờ St Lawrence). Q7: `had been finished` ↔ `almost-completed`.

sents: In 1892 Henderson accepted a full-time position with the CPR as manager of a photographic department which he was to set up and administer.
His duties included spending four months in the field each year.
That summer he made his second trip west, photographing extensively along the railway line as far as Victoria.
He continued in this post until 1897, when he retired completely from photography.

simp.text: Henderson accepted a full-time position with the CPR
simp.note: Bỏ as manager…, which he was to…

simp.text: duties included four months in the field
he made his second trip west
He continued until 1897, retired from photography

paras.conn: ① nhận việc CPR → ② nhiệm vụ → ③ chuyến đi phía tây → ④ làm đến 1897 rồi nghỉ hẳn. Mạch: **vị trí cuối cùng → nghỉ hẳn**.
paras.main: Henderson **làm cho CPR đến 1897 rồi giải nghệ**.

sents: When Henderson died in 1913, his huge collection of glass negatives was stored in the basement of his house.
Today collections of his work are held at the National Archives of Canada, Ottawa, and the McCord Museum of Canadian History, Montreal.

simp.text: collection was stored in the basement
collections are held at the Archives and the Museum

paras.main: Ảnh của ông **được lưu ở các tổ chức** ngày nay. (Không có câu hỏi.)

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? In boxes 1-8 on your answer sheet, write

items.q: Henderson rarely visited the area around Press estate when he was younger.
items.exp:
> đoạn 1 ⑤ …Alexander **spent much of his childhood in the area**, playing on the beach near Eyemouth or fishing in the streams nearby. đoạn 2 ① …Henderson **returned to Press at weekends.**

`rarely visited` ↔ `spent much of his childhood`, `returned … at weekends`. Ngược.

items.q: Henderson pursued a business career because it was what his family wanted.
items.exp:
> đoạn 2 ③ Although he never liked the prospect of a business career, **he stayed with it to please his family.**

`pursued a business career` = `stayed with it`; `because it was what his family wanted` = `to please his family`.
💡 `Although A, B`: A (`never liked`) là điều **không thích**, B (`stayed with it to please his family`) là **lý do thật**.
pairs: because it was what his family wanted

items.q: Henderson and Notman were surprised by the results of their 1865 experiment.
items.exp:
> đoạn 3 ③ …they **cooperated on experiments with magnesium flares** as a source of artificial light in 1865.

Bài chỉ nói họ **hợp tác thí nghiệm**, không nói **kết quả** hay **cảm xúc ngạc nhiên**.

| Mắt thông tin | Bài có không? |
|---|---|
| thí nghiệm 1865 | ✓ |
| **họ ngạc nhiên vì kết quả** | ✗ |

items.q: There were many similarities between Henderson's early landscapes and those of Notman.
items.exp:
> đoạn 4 ① In spite of their friendship, **their styles of photography were quite different.** ② While Notman's landscapes were noted for their **bold realism**, Henderson … produced **romantic images**…

`many similarities` ↔ `quite different`.
⚠️ Hai người là bạn thân (đoạn 3) nhưng `In spite of their friendship` báo hiệu **phong cách khác**.

items.q: The studio that Henderson opened in 1866 was close to his home.
items.exp: Đoạn 5 ① chỉ nói `gave up his business to open a photographic studio`. **Không** nói vị trí.

items.q: Henderson gave up portraiture so that he could focus on taking photographs of scenery.
items.exp:
> đoạn 5 ② From about 1870 **he dropped portraiture to specialize in landscape photography and other views.**

`gave up portraiture` = `dropped portraiture`; `so that he could focus on … scenery` = `to specialize in landscape photography`.
pairs: so that he could focus on … scenery

items.q: When Henderson began work for the Intercolonial Railway, the Montreal to Halifax line had been finished.
items.exp:
> đoạn 7 ⑤ This undertaking led in 1875 to a commission … along the **almost-completed line** connecting Montreal to Halifax.

`had been finished` ↔ `almost-completed`. Chưa xong.
⚠️ Năm 1872 ông chụp ảnh **xây dựng** (④), năm 1875 mới nhận ủy thác; dù mốc nào cũng chưa hoàn tất.

items.q: Henderson's last work as a photographer was with the Canadian Pacific Railway.
items.exp:
> đoạn 8 ① In 1892 Henderson accepted a full-time position with the CPR… ④ **He continued in this post until 1897, when he retired completely from photography.**

`last work` = công việc cuối trước khi `retired completely`.

passages.title: Back to the future of skyscraper design
footnote: * pathogens: microorganisms that can cause disease

paras.label: A
sents: The Recovery of Natural Environments in Architecture by Professor Alan Short is the culmination of 30 years of research and award-winning green building design by Short and colleagues…
'The crisis in building design is already here,' said Short.
'Policy makers think you can solve energy and building problems with gadgets. You can't.'
'As global temperatures continue to rise, we are going to continue to squander more and more energy on keeping our buildings mechanically cool until we have run out of capacity.'

simp.text: The Recovery… is the culmination of 30 years of research
crisis is already here
Policy makers think gadgets solve problems; You can't
simp.note: You can't phủ định ý trước

simp.text: we continue to squander more energy on cooling

paras.conn: ① cuốn sách → ② khủng hoảng đã đến → ③ chính sách dựa vào "gadget" là sai → ④ hậu quả: lãng phí điện.
paras.main: Short cảnh báo **khủng hoảng thiết kế và lãng phí năng lượng**.

paras.label: B
sents: Short is calling for a sweeping reinvention of how skyscrapers and major public buildings are designed – to end the reliance on sealed buildings which exist solely via the 'life support' system of vast air conditioning units.

Instead, he shows it is entirely possible to accommodate natural ventilation and cooling in large buildings by looking into the past, before the widespread introduction of air conditioning systems, which were 'relentlessly and aggressively marketed' by their inventors.

simp.text: Short is calling for a reinvention
he shows natural ventilation is possible by looking into the past; AC systems were 'relentlessly and aggressively marketed'
simp.note: Giữ mệnh đề which were… vì Q18

paras.conn: ① cần đổi cách thiết kế → ② `Instead`: dùng thông gió tự nhiên, nhìn về quá khứ; điều hòa từng được tiếp thị mạnh.
paras.main: Short muốn **thay điều hòa bằng thông gió tự nhiên**.

paras.label: C
sents: Short points out that to make most contemporary buildings habitable, they have to be sealed and air conditioned.
The energy use and carbon emissions this generates is spectacular and largely unnecessary.
Buildings in the West account for 40-50% of electricity usage, generating substantial carbon emissions, and the rest of the world is catching up at a frightening rate.
Short regards glass, steel and air-conditioned skyscrapers as symbols of status, rather than practical ways of meeting our requirements.

simp.text: buildings have to be sealed and air conditioned
energy use is spectacular and largely unnecessary
Buildings account for 40–50% of electricity
Short regards skyscrapers as symbols of status
simp.note: Giữ symbols of status; rather than = phủ định phần sau

paras.conn: ① tòa nhà phải kín → ② tốn điện lớn → ③ chiếm 40–50% → ④ nguyên nhân sâu: nhà cao là biểu tượng, không thực dụng.
paras.main: Tòa nhà hiện đại **tốn điện** và nhà chọc trời là **biểu tượng địa vị**.

paras.label: D
sents: Short's book highlights a developing and sophisticated art and science of ventilating buildings through the 19th and earlier-20th centuries, including the design of ingeniously ventilated hospitals.
Of particular interest were those built to the designs of John Shaw Billings, including the first Johns Hopkins Hospital in the US city of Baltimore (1873-1889).
'We spent three years digitally modelling Billings' final designs,' says Short.
'We put pathogens in the airstreams, modelled for someone with tuberculosis (TB) coughing in the wards and we found the ventilation systems in the room would have kept other patients safe from harm.'

simp.text: book highlights an art and science of ventilating buildings
simp.note: Giữ design of … hospitals vì Q19

simp.text: those were of interest, built to the designs of Billings
We spent three years digitally modelling designs
We put pathogens in airstreams; found ventilation would have kept patients safe

paras.conn: ① nghệ thuật thông gió thế kỷ 19 → ② tiêu biểu: thiết kế của Billings → ③ mô hình hóa 3 năm → ④ thử mầm bệnh: thông gió bảo vệ bệnh nhân.
paras.main: Short **mô hình hóa thiết kế của Billings** và thấy thông gió **giữ an toàn** cho bệnh nhân.
warn: ⚠️ Q17 hỏi **cách thử** (D), không phải kết quả 24 lần/giờ (E).

paras.label: E
sents: 'We discovered that 19th-century hospital wards could generate up to 24 air changes an hour – that's similar to the performance of a modern-day, computer-controlled operating theatre.
We believe you could build wards based on these principles now.
Single rooms are not appropriate for all patients.
Communal wards appropriate for certain patients – older people with dementia, for example – would work just as well in today's hospitals, at a fraction of the energy cost.'

Professor Short contends the mindset and skill-sets behind these designs have been completely lost, lamenting the disappearance of expertly designed theatres, opera houses, and other buildings where up to half the volume of the building was given over to ensuring everyone got fresh air.

simp.text: wards could generate 24 air changes an hour (similar to a modern operating theatre)
you could build wards
Single rooms are not appropriate
Communal wards would work just as well, at a fraction of the energy cost
Short contends the mindset has been lost

paras.conn: ① thông gió xưa tốt như phòng mổ → ② xây lại được → ③④ phòng chung phù hợp hơn và tiết kiệm → ⑤ nhưng kiến thức đã mất.
paras.main: Thông gió thế kỷ 19 **ngang chuẩn hiện đại**, phòng chung **tiết kiệm năng lượng**.

paras.label: F
sents: Much of the ingenuity present in 19th-century hospital and building design was driven by a panicked public clamouring for buildings that could protect against what was thought to be the lethal threat of miasmas – toxic air that spread disease.

Miasmas were feared as the principal agents of disease and epidemics for centuries, and were used to explain the spread of infection from the Middle Ages right through to the cholera outbreaks in London and Paris during the 1850s.
Foul air, rather than germs, was believed to be the main driver of 'hospital fever', leading to disease and frequent death.
The prosperous steered clear of hospitals.
While miasma theory has been long since disproved, Short has for the last 30 years advocated a return to some of the building design principles produced in its wake.

simp.text: ingenuity was driven by a panicked public clamouring for protection against miasmas
simp.note: Giữ public, miasmas vì Q24, Q25

simp.text: Miasmas were feared; were used to explain infection up to the cholera outbreaks
Foul air was believed to be the main driver of 'hospital fever'
The prosperous steered clear of hospitals
Short has advocated a return to principles

paras.conn: ① nỗi sợ khí độc thúc đẩy thiết kế → ② khí độc bị sợ hàng thế kỷ → ③④ nên người giàu tránh bệnh viện → ⑤ thuyết sai nhưng nguyên tắc thiết kế vẫn đáng dùng.
paras.main: **Nỗi sợ miasma** khiến người ta tránh bệnh viện và thúc đẩy thiết kế thông gió.

paras.label: G
sents: Today, huge amounts of a building's space and construction cost are given over to air conditioning.
'But I have designed and built a series of buildings over the past three decades which have tried to reinvent some of these ideas and then measure what happens.
To go forward into our new low-energy, low-carbon future, we would be well advised to look back at design before our high-energy, high-carbon present appeared.
What is surprising is what a rich legacy we have abandoned.'

simp.text: space and cost are given over to AC
I have designed and built buildings
we would be well advised to look back
What is surprising is the rich legacy we have abandoned

paras.main: Muốn tương lai ít carbon thì **nên học từ thiết kế trước đây**. (Không có câu hỏi.)

paras.label: H
sents: Successful examples of Short's approach include the Queen's Building at De Montfort University in Leicester.

Containing as many as 2,000 staff and students, the entire building is naturally ventilated, passively cooled and naturally lit, including the two largest auditoria, each seating more than 150 people.
The award-winning building uses a fraction of the electricity of comparable buildings in the UK.

Short contends that glass skyscrapers in London and around the world will become a liability over the next 20 or 30 years if climate modelling predictions and energy price rises come to pass as expected.

simp.text: examples include the Queen's Building
building is naturally ventilated, cooled and lit
building uses a fraction of the electricity
Short contends glass skyscrapers will become a liability

paras.main: Queen's Building **chứng minh** cách tiếp cận này. (Không có câu hỏi.)

paras.label: I
sents: He is convinced that sufficiently cooled skyscrapers using the natural environment can be produced in almost any climate.

He and his team have worked on hybrid buildings in the harsh climates of Beijing and Chicago – built with natural ventilation assisted by back-up air conditioning – which, surprisingly perhaps, can be switched off more than half the time on milder days and during the spring and autumn.
Short looks at how we might reimagine the cities, offices and homes of the future. Maybe it's time we changed our outlook.

simp.text: He is convinced skyscrapers can be produced
He and team have worked on hybrid buildings
Short looks at how we might reimagine

paras.main: Cách này **áp dụng được ở nhiều khí hậu**. (Không có câu hỏi.)

paras.label: A
sents: Organisation is big business.
Whether it is of our lives – all those inboxes and calendars – or how companies are structured, a multi-billion dollar industry helps to meet this need.
We have more strategies for time management, project management and self-organisation than at any other time in human history.
We are told that we ought to organize our company, our home life, our week, our day and even our sleep, all as a means to becoming more productive.
Every week, countless seminars and workshops take place around the world to tell a paying public that they ought to structure their lives in order to achieve this.
This rhetoric has also crept into the thinking of business leaders and entrepreneurs, much to the delight of self-proclaimed perfectionists with the need to get everything right.
The number of business schools and graduates has massively increased over the past 50 years, essentially teaching people how to organise well.

A large proportion of workers from all demographics claim to be dissatisfied with the way their work is structured and the way they are managed.

paras.label: D
sents: New research suggests that this obsession with efficiency is misguided.
The problem is not necessarily the management theories or strategies we use to organise our work; it's the basic assumptions we hold in approaching how we work.

This assumption has also fostered the idea that disorder must be detrimental to organizational productivity.

paras.label: G
sents: In recent times companies have slowly started to embrace this disorganisation.
Many of them embrace it in terms of perception (embracing the idea of disorder, as opposed to fearing it) and in terms of process (putting mechanisms in place to reduce structure).
For example, Oticon, a large Danish manufacturer of hearing aids, used what it called a 'spaghetti' structure in order to reduce the organisation's rigid hierarchies.
This involved scrapping formal job titles and giving staff huge amounts of ownership over their own time and projects.
This approach proved to be highly successful initially, with clear improvements in worker productivity in all facets of the business.
In similar fashion, the former chairman of General Electric embraced disorganisation, putting forward the idea of the 'boundaryless' organisation.
Again, it involves breaking down the barriers between different parts of a company and encouraging virtual collaboration and flexible working.
Google and a number of other tech companies have embraced (at least in part) these kinds of flexible structures, facilitated by technology and strong company values which glue people together.

items.q: Section E

## Phần A – Simplify 15 câu (tìm [S][V], bỏ phần phụ)

1. Although he never liked the prospect of a business career, he stayed with it to please his family.
2. While Notman's landscapes were noted for their bold realism, Henderson for the first 20 years of his career produced romantic images, showing the strong influence of the British landscape tradition.
3. This approach proved to be highly successful initially, with clear improvements in worker productivity in all facets of the business.
4. There was little competing hobby or amateur photography before the late 1880s because of the time-consuming techniques involved and the weight of equipment.
5. This undertaking led in 1875 to a commission from the railway to record the principal structures along the almost-completed line connecting Montreal to Halifax.
6. Instead, he shows it is entirely possible to accommodate natural ventilation and cooling in large buildings by looking into the past.
7. Short regards glass, steel and air-conditioned skyscrapers as symbols of status, rather than practical ways of meeting our requirements.
8. 'We put pathogens in the airstreams, modelled for someone with tuberculosis coughing in the wards.'
9. Single rooms are not appropriate for all patients.
10. Foul air, rather than germs, was believed to be the main driver of 'hospital fever'.
11. While miasma theory has been long since disproved, Short has advocated a return to some of the building design principles produced in its wake.
12. The problem is not necessarily the management theories we use; it's the basic assumptions we hold in approaching how we work.
13. The result is that businesses and people spend time and money organising themselves for the sake of organising, rather than actually looking at the end goal.
14. Order does increase productivity to a certain extent, but eventually the benefit it yields reduces until further order reduces productivity.
15. In fact, research shows that, when innovating, the best approach is to create an environment devoid of structure and hierarchy.

## Phần B – Read connection (trả lời bằng 1–2 câu)

1. Passage 1, đoạn 4: câu ① và ② nối với nhau bằng cách nào? Vì sao ② giúp trả lời Q4?

method:
1. **Đọc câu hỏi, xác định cấu trúc.** Ô trống cần từ loại gì? Câu hỏi khẳng định điều gì?
2. **Định vị** bằng từ khóa *không paraphrase được* (tên riêng, số, năm).
3. **Simplify**: tìm [S]–[V], bỏ mệnh đề quan hệ, V-ing/V-ed, ngoặc, liệt kê, cụm đưa tin.
4. **So ý, không so chữ.**

| Dạng | Nguyên tắc |
|---|---|
| T/F/NG | Tách **mắt thông tin**; FALSE = nói **ngược**; NG = **thiếu** mắt |
| Notes/Summary completion | **Từ loại** + **giới hạn số từ** trước; lấy **nguyên văn** từ bài |
| Matching Information | Xác định **loại thông tin** rồi tìm đoạn |
| Matching Headings | Heading = **ý chính cả đoạn**; có heading thừa |

extras.title: 6 LỖI TƯ DUY CẦN BỎ
extras.md:
1. **Chộp từ giống, bỏ qua mắt thông tin.** Q3 (`experiments` có nhưng thiếu "ngạc nhiên"), Q5 (`studio` có nhưng thiếu vị trí).
2. **Bỏ sót tín hiệu đảo chiều.** Q2 (`Although`), Q4 (`In spite of their friendship`).
3. **Nhầm "kết quả" với "cách làm".** Q17 (D) vs Q16 (E).
4. **Chọn heading theo chi tiết.** Q33 (G có `highly successful` ⇒ dễ chọn v), Q34.
5. **Dùng chi tiết lân cận.** Q12 (`yacht` vs `canoe`), Q23 (`single` vs `communal`).
6. **Suy ra quan hệ nhân quả không có.** Q40 (`In similar fashion` ≠ `inspired by`).

extras.title: BÀI TẬP TỰ LUYỆN (1 tuần)
extras.md:
- **Ngày 1–2:** chép 12 verb pattern, đặt 1 câu cho mỗi pattern.
- **Ngày 3:** làm lại Q1–8; mỗi câu viết *"bài nói ___ / câu hỏi nói ___"*.
- **Ngày 4:** làm lại Q14–18: ghi **loại thông tin** cần tìm trước khi đọc đoạn.
- **Ngày 5:** làm lại Q9–13, Q19–26, Q35–37; ghi từ loại + từ khóa quanh ô trống.
- **Ngày 6:** làm lại Q27–34: **gạch ý chính từng đoạn** trước khi nhìn heading, rồi loại heading thừa.
- **Ngày 7:** làm Cam 14 Test 3 Passage 1 (20 phút); ghi sổ lỗi theo 6 lỗi trên.

### Sổ lỗi

Ghi mỗi câu sai vào một dòng với 1 trong 8 nhóm: thiếu từ vựng · không nhận ra paraphrase · hiểu sai nội dung · nhầm T/F/NG · xác định sai từ khóa · quản lý thời gian · hiểu sai yêu cầu · suy diễn quá mức.

Khi bạn gửi bài làm, mình sẽ chấm, phân loại lỗi, chỉ ra 3 điểm yếu lớn nhất và đề xuất bài kế tiếp.
